camera: Sony A7III, multispectral conversion (internal IR filter stack removed, sensor cover glass replaced with fused silica; colour filter array intact)
source: Crowther, J. Monochrome Camera Conversion: Effect on Sensitivity for Multispectral Imaging (Ultraviolet, Visible, and Infrared). J. Imaging 2022, 8, 54. https://doi.org/10.3390/jimaging8030054 (CC BY 4.0), Figure 1f
method: Traced programmatically from Figure 1f (raster at 185 ppi): axes calibrated from the tick labels (0-14000 response, 300-800nm), each channel isolated by its line colour and read at every 20nm data point. The author's own measurements are within 3% between repeats; this trace adds roughly +/-1 px (about 50 response units, under 0.5% of full scale). At local peaks and troughs the vertex is read at the line edge (half a line width in) rather than the column median, which would cut peaks short.
occluded: Where another line is drawn on top, the point was read from the visible antialiased edge (R 340, 380, 400nm and G 800nm, read 4px inside the axis) or, where nothing shows, interpolated: R 300nm, R 320nm, B 300nm, B 320nm (all below 2% of full scale).
green: Green is the paper's Green2 channel; Green1 is drawn underneath it and the two coincide.
